problem: An opener-raised HTTPError owns a response outside the successful response context; the current retry owner does not explicitly retire it before continuation. Source observation alone does not certify a runtime leak.
required_behavior: Close opener-raised HTTPError before decision, Retry-After parsing, sleep, redispatch or terminal return/raise.
Preserve unchanged request object, GET-only admission, retry taxonomy and existing response status/headers.
Successful responses remain caller-owned and are returned without premature close.
Cleanup failure raises typed ProviderReadError, chains the original HTTPError and records the secondary cleanup exception type; no sleep or redispatch.
Cancellation during cleanup or backoff propagates unchanged and never permits another dispatch; interrupted cleanup is not successful retirement.
Do not read discarded error bodies, retry mutations, change public CLI/status identity or infer authority from observations.
cause_specific_controls: 429 and503: actual response body closes before sleeper and same-object second dispatch.
401 and404: original HTTPError object/status preserved after body close.
Invalid Retry-After: body closes before typed parsing rejection; zero continuation.
Exhaustion: all three actual error bodies close; exact final HTTPError remains chained cause.
Close OSError: one dispatch, no sleep, typed cleanup block with original HTTPError and secondary type.
Interrupted backoff: body already closed, same cancellation propagated, one dispatch.
Interrupted close: same cancellation propagated with HTTPError context, one dispatch; no successful cleanup claim.
Actual urllib HTTPError.fp is closed before sleep and second same-object request, for429/503 overHTTP and verifiedTLS using existing fixture; four authored cases.
implementation_sequence: Commit this bounded contract and failing behavioral controls before production delta.
